ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In a uniform magnetic field, a closed rectangular metal coil of 100 turns rotates at a uniform speed around a fixed axis perpendicular to the magnetic induction lines, and the magnetic flux passing through this coil changes with time according to the sinusoidal law shown in the diagram. Suppose the total resistance of the coil is 2 Ω, then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Dataset Open Question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: According to the sinusoidal change law of magnetic flux with time shown in the diagram, at t＝0, what is the positional relationship between the plane of the coil and the magnetic induction lines?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: The coil plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to the sinusoidal change law of magnetic flux with time shown in the diagram, at t＝0, what is the positional relationship between the plane of the coil and the magnetic induction lines?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The coil plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled Φ/Wb, the horizontal axis is labeled t/s, and the magnetic flux changes sinusoidally with time. The curve starts from the coordinate origin at t=0, when Φ=0; subsequently it reaches +0.04 Wb at about 0.5 s, and reaches -0.04 Wb at about 1.5 s. Then reason: When the coil rotates in a uniform magnetic field, the magnetic flux passing through the coil can be written as Φ=BS cosθ, where θ is the angle between the direction of the magnetic field lines and the normal to the coil plane. At t=0, the image shows Φ=0, so cosθ=0, that is θ=90°, indicating that the direction of the magnetic field lines is perpendicular to the normal of the coil plane. Therefore the magnetic field lines are parallel to the coil plane.
